headline: NARROWS INFERNO: 40 Blocks Ash, 12,000 Displaced Overnight
body:
A fire that ignited in the lower Narrows district around 0200 hours Wednesday has consumed forty contiguous city blocks, reducing an estimated 6,800 residential units to scorched steel and carbonized concrete. Emergency responders from Ferrogate Transit's contracted fire suppression crews arrived nearly ninety minutes after the first distress calls — a delay residents say is criminal. Casualty figures remain in flux, with Meridian Emergency Services citing 312 confirmed dead and over 800 still unaccounted for as of this broadcast. The blaze is believed to have originated near the Tessera-operated power relay station on Culvert Row, though Tessera's communications office has already issued a pre-emptive denial.

Survivors gathered at the Geartown overflow shelters describe scenes of utter chaos — stairwells melting, fire suppression systems that never activated, BCI emergency alert protocols that broadcast in Axiom-licensed frequency bands inaccessible to the Narrows' older-model implants. 'My kids didn't get a single alarm ping,' said Dara Mwangi-Sousa, 38, who lost her youngest daughter in the collapse of the Culvert Row tenements. 'Not one. Because we can't afford the NovaMind subscription tier that carries emergency services.'

The Collective has dispatched aid teams and is calling for an independent investigation into Tessera's relay infrastructure, which residents allege has been running at unsafe thermal loads for over two years following cost-cutting maintenance deferrals. Federal Remnant housing authority has promised temporary shelter vouchers — redeemable at Axiom-certified facilities only, none of which are located within the Narrows. The Iron Lotus is reportedly already moving to fill the vacuum, distributing water and nutrient packs from unmarked vehicles throughout the displaced population zones.
aftermath: A Federal Remnant inquiry was opened and quietly closed eighteen months later without findings; Tessera paid a 40,000 quanta regulatory fine — less than the cost of the relay station itself.
runner_relevance: The displacement of 12,000 residents and the power vacuum left in the Narrows created immediate demand for runners across multiple contract types: Iron Lotus hired couriers and protection details to secure their aid-distribution territory against rivals; The Collective contracted data-retrieval runners to pull Tessera's internal maintenance logs before they could be wiped; displaced residents and small operators paid for extraction runs to recover valuables and documents from still-smoldering structures before Tessera's private security cordoned the zone. A secondary market emerged for runners who could navigate Axiom shelter bureaucracy and smuggle people into non-Axiom housing illegally.
